page: Amazon Web Services r7g.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the custom ARMv8 AWS Graviton3 architecture with Neoverse-V1 cores. The instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores (4 vCPUs) operating at 2.6 GHz, with a 1:1 physical core-to-thread topology. Cache provisioning includes 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per core ratio. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, and it provides a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate competitive performance in memory-intensive scenarios, reflected in a PassMark memory score that falls within the top 25% of tested systems. Read memory bandwidth achieves 385.82 GB/sec for small cached blocks (16 KB) and 97.0 GB/sec for large blocks (256 MB), alongside 39.6 GB/sec for uncached write operations. General computational metrics, including Geekbench single-core (1494.0) and multi-core (4847.0) alongside stress-ng results, sit within the middle 50% average tier. Application-level metrics register 6.63 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 8.32 GB/sec throughput in static web serving.

Performance tradeoffs emerge primarily in floating-point, vectorized, and specialized instruction sets. PassMark CPU scores place in the bottom 25%, with the extended instructions test and ray tracing falling into weak tiers, and the PassMark encryption test falling to the bottom 10%. Without dedicated GPU hardware or advanced x86 matrix extensions, large language model inference is constrained, measuring 44.27 tokens/sec on 135M parameter models and 6.02 tokens/sec on 7B models.

With its 8:1 memory-to-core ratio and strong memory subsystem, the r7g.xlarge delivers solid operational efficiency for workloads prioritizing RAM capacity over raw floating-point compute. It is well-fitted for in-memory databases such as Redis, caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, data preprocessing, and memory-intensive microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services r7g.xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by a 4-core, 4-vCPU ARMv8 AWS Graviton3 processor using Neoverse-V1 cores clocked at 2.6 GHz. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features 32.0 GB of dedicated system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance lacks bundled local storage and discrete GPUs, maintaining a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. In benchmark evaluations, memory throughput ranks in the top 25%, with Redis SET operations sustaining 6.63 million operations per second and cached memory reads reaching 385.82 GB/sec. Computational and encryption performance are comparatively lower, rendering the server ineffective for heavy cryptographic calculations or machine learning inference. The r7g.xlarge is targeted toward memory-heavy applications, including in-memory caches, key-value datastores, relational databases, and high-throughput memory-bound backend services.
